items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: He's got real flexible wrists like the great Art Blakely, who was in Fletcher's band for a long time and I had the pleasure of being part of that rhythm section

ctx.x: He does that with his voice, while holding his flute, all the same time. And then he'll play a little riff, and he'll get to moving, you know, and get the people swinging, you know, and he says, "Now I don't want you girls to get excited behind this," he says. "I see it's getting to you." So he talks -- he's funny, you know, and it -- you know, he sells it.

And I've got an excellent little drummer with me, named Randy Carroll, and, thank God, he doesn't play loud, extra loud. He can. On of his solos -- he has a few things that he does by himself; (unintelligible) sometimes, and he keeps steady time. He's got real flexible wrists like the great Art Blakely, who was in Fletcher's band for a long time and I had the pleasure of being part of that rhythm section,

and he likes it a lot, and he plays real good. And he uses his brushes on things like that. When he first came into the group, he respected my judgment. He said, "How do you want me to do this, (Unintelligible) do a solo, so we did get a few things together. And we stopped and we talked, and I said, "I'd like this," you know, so and so.
